title: after-hours-staggered-weight-deploy-flap-incident-review
body:
Summary:

At ~02:13 UTC on 2026-03-11 we observed a multi-region degradation in model responses after a staggered weight rollout to the preview cohort (preview routing = 5% of traffic). Symptoms were subtle first (increased decode retries, small spike in token-level latency) then progressed to increased 500s and client-observed truncation on long contexts. Impact lasted ~42 minutes for a subset of requests routed through two edge regions before automatic fallback to the previous model variant completed.

What happened (high level):
- We executed a rolling weight deployment that intentionally applied weight shards in a staggered order to reduce peak IO.
- Due to an interaction between the staggered apply order and KV-cache prewarm, some serving nodes accepted new weight metadata while others still held old tokenizer-compatibility metadata derived from the previous manifest.
- A small percentage of routed requests hit a mixed-state path: the model weights were new but token-id mapping (subtoken map + eos offsets) came from the old artifact. That produced decoding misalignment (low-prob EOS placement) and longer generation loops, which pushed request durations past SLO and triggered gateway 500s on the client side.

Technical timeline (reconstructed):
- 02:07 UTC: rollout start (shard apply orchestration kicked off with staggered windows).
- 02:12 UTC: first signs in internal trace: anomalous decode latency for preview cohort requests (SRE-4821).
- 02:13 UTC: error budget alarm for preview route; ops channel notified.
- 02:18 UTC: Ops initiated partial traffic re-route off preview cohort to stable model; some requests still land on mixed-state machines due to routing cache TTLs.
- 02:25 UTC: automated fallback for route completed for majority; manual intervention to drain remaining mixed nodes.
- 02:55 UTC: all nodes confirmed healthy; full telemetry returned to baseline.

Root cause hypothesis: weight manifest and tokenizer metadata were updated in two separate steps; the staggered apply left a window where weight version and tokenizer/versioned-vocab were inconsistent. The runtime assumes atomic co-deployment of weights + tokenizer metadata for safe decode; here the orchestration order broke that assumption. Secondary contributors: aggressive KV-cache eviction on a subset of nodes caused them to request metadata from the control plane at slightly different times, expanding the inconsistent window.

Why this escaped preview safety nets:
- Preview cohort traffic rate is low; early detectability relied on token-level latencies that were masked by batching variance.
- Health checks were focused on binary correctness (model responded) and high-level latency percentiles; they did not include token-alignment or EOS placement assertions.

Immediate mitigations taken:
- Stopped the rollout and re-pointed preview routing to stable model variant (completed by 02:18 UTC).
- Evicted preview cohort service peer nodes from LB and forced a coordinated restart to clear mixed metadata.
- Added an ad-hoc check that compared model weight checksum vs tokenizer metadata checksum during health probes for all preview machines while investigating.

Longer-term action items (recommended and owners):
- Require atomic publish for weight bundle + tokenizer metadata in the deployment orchestration. Owner: eng-serving-runtime (PR opened: runtime/pull/1583).
- Add token-alignment canary tests that run a small set of deterministically seeded decode checks post-deploy and fail-fast if alignment deviates. Owner: site-reliability-engineering + applied-ml.
- Harden KV-cache priming: ensure control-plane emits a "bundle ready" marker only after all nodes have confirmed receipt; modify cache TTLs for metadata requests to reduce split-brain windows. Owner: infra.
- Update runbook: include an explicit step to verify tokenizer and weight manifest checksums match before shifting any traffic. Owner: svcs-runbooks.
- Add alerting for token-level anomalies (unexpected EOS-probability shift / decode loop increases) and create dashboard panels showing model-weight vs tokenizer-version parity. Owner: observability.

Runbook changes (draft):
- Pre-deploy checks: verify bundle contains both weights and tokenizer files, compute and store combined-bundle-checksum.
- Deploy step: apply bundle atomically or stage with bundle-lock=on so routing controller delays traffic until lock cleared.
- Post-apply verification: run short seeded decode (3 inputs) and compare output tokenization indices to baseline. Fail and halt rollout on mismatch.
- Recovery guidance: if mixed-state is suspected: drain affected nodes, restart runtime with forced metadata refresh, and re-validate seeded decode before re-introducing to LB.

Open questions / unknowns:
- Why did only two regions observe the extended window? Hypothesis: those regions had synchronized KV-cache eviction policy due to a recent infra config push — need infra audit logs.
- Is there a performance regression introduced by adding atomic bundle-lock? We need a perf test in release pipeline.

Artifacts and links: see linked_artifacts for tickets/PRs. Traces are in Tempo: trace ids -> SRE-4821-TRACE-02 and SRE-4821-TRACE-03.

Post-incident retrospective notes:
- Preview cohorts are useful but we overestimated the ability of percent-based routing to isolate stateful rollout assumptions.
- Deployment orchestration must treat tokenizer metadata as first-class citizen when model artifacts are stateful and affect decoding semantics.
- Small deterministic decode checks catch semantic regressions faster than percentile-based latency alarms.

Next steps (owners and ETA):
- Merge atomic bundle publish in runtime orchestration (eng-serving-runtime) — ETA 2 weeks.
- Add token-alignment canary harness and alert (applied-ml + observability) — ETA 3 weeks.
- Update runbook and run an internal tabletop simulation of a staggered deploy (SRE + runtime) — ETA 1 week.

Notes to on-call: if you suspect mixed-state on a live rollout: do not immediately roll back; prefer draining affected nodes and verifying decode parity on a drained node before reintroducing. Rolling back without fixing metadata parity can reintroduce mismatch in reverse direction.

Document history: initial draft by Aisha Patel 2026-03-11; reviewers Miguel Ortega, Rina Shah, Samir Bose.
